objectives.description: Describe Greek life and achievements and their influence on the western world
Explain the significance of Athenian democracy and compare it to systems of government today
Evaluate the lasting influence of Ancient Greek achievements (democracy, philosophy, theatre, the Olympics) on the modern world, using evidence
Describe Anglo-Saxon settlement of Britain and everyday Anglo-Saxon life
Explain the significance of Anglo-Saxon kingdoms, laws and the spread of Christianity
Compare different types of historical sources (artefacts, written accounts, archaeology) about Anglo-Saxon Britain and evaluate their reliability
Describe Viking and Anglo-Saxon struggles for the Kingdom of England
Use evidence from artefacts and sources to describe Viking exploration and settlement
Explain the significance of key events in the Viking and Anglo-Saxon struggle for England, including the eventual Norman Conquest of 1066

strands.name: The Second World War
strands.description: New for Y6: a study of a significant turning point in twentieth-century British history.

objectives.description: Describe the causes and key events of the Second World War, including the Blitz and evacuation
Describe everyday life on the home front, including rationing and the role of women in the war effort
Use a range of sources (photographs, ration books, propaganda posters) to draw conclusions about life during the war

strands.name: Crime and Punishment Through Time
strands.description: New for Y6: a thematic study of how crime, punishment and law have changed across different periods studied.

objectives.description: Describe how crime and punishment changed from Anglo-Saxon times to the present day
Explain reasons for changes in attitudes to crime and punishment over time, linking them to wider social change
